title: Dhruv Rathee Detained, CJP Leaders Held as Delhi Blocks October 10 Jantar Mantar Protest
excerpt: Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at IGI Airport and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee at his Gurugram home on Saturday, preempting the party's unpermitted protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over electoral-roll revision.
body:
• YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at his Gurugram residence on Saturday morning after refusing police requests to stay away from the Cockroach Janta Party's Jantar Mantar protest, for which permission was denied.
  • CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka were detained at IGI Airport shortly after landing; police sources say around 150 protesters have been detained across New Delhi.
  • The protest targets Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
  • Delhi remains sealed around the protest site: mobile internet blocked in a 4-km zone near Janpath-Kartavya Path, 57 metro stations with closed entry/exit gates, and 10 temporary detention centers in operation.

A protest stopped before it started

The Cockroach Janta Party's planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar never got a chance to begin. Delhi Police denied permission for the protest earlier in the week, citing security considerations — and on Saturday morning, they moved to prevent its leaders and supporters from reaching the site at all.

https://x.com/timesofindia/status/2108816940013961241

The party said its top leaders — Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka — were detained at Indira Gandhi International Airport shortly after their flight landed in the capital. The CJP described the detentions as a planned move to stop its leaders from reaching the protest site, calling it a violation of freedom of movement and demanding their immediate release.

Rathee detained at home

The day's most prominent detention was YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, detained at his family residence in Kendriya Vihar society, Gurugram's Sector 56. A senior Gurugram police official said a Delhi Police team reached his home on Saturday morning and urged him not to travel to the national capital for the unpermitted protest, with Gurugram police joining the effort.

"However, we were forced to detain him after he turned down all the requests not to travel to Delhi. We would have preferred not to detain him in case Rathee had listened to the law enforcement agencies."

— Senior Gurugram police official, quoted by Hindustan Times

Rathee, who is based in Germany and had recently traveled to India, had posted videos asking supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar on Saturday. Police personnel remain stationed at his residence until further orders, officials said.

The crackdown extended beyond the party's leadership. CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh was detained, along with content creator Kavya Karnatac, who posts under the Instagram handle 'kk.create,' in Dhaula Kuan. According to PTI, police have detained around 150 protesters from various locations across the New Delhi area.

The fortified capital

The detentions unfolded against an extraordinary security lockdown. Authorities blocked mobile internet services within a 4-kilometer radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path intersection, shut entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations, and set up 10 temporary detention centers across the capital to manage crowd movement. Reports earlier in the week described 11 layers of barricades around Jantar Mantar.

The CJP responded on X: "The Dictator is TERRIFIED of young people who question its wrongdoings and refuse to stay silent!" The party condemned what it called a citywide crackdown designed to silence democratic dissent and said its agitation would continue regardless of the leadership's detention.

Why they are protesting

The proposed demonstration targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and changes to Form 6, used for voter registration. The party has demanded the CEC's resignation, a freeze on upcoming elections, and an independent audit of the SIR voter rolls.

Congress leaders have weighed in on the heavy security deployment: Mallikarjun Kharge invoked the Sholay dialogue "jo aadmi darta hai" to accuse the government of fear, while Shashi Tharoor called the Delhi curbs "regressive."

What to watch

The immediate question is whether any protesters make it to Jantar Mantar at all, given the detentions and the sealed perimeter. The longer arc is legal: opposition parties and civil society groups have already approached the courts over the protest curbs, and how judges rule on preventive detention for an unpermitted political demonstration will shape the space for street protest in the capital through the election season.
